items.title: Victorian election 2026 live: voters head to the polls as Coalition seeks to topple Labor – latest news
paragraphs: ‘Greens surge is coming’, Victorian leader says

The Victorian Greens leader, Ellen Sandell, told ABC’s Weekend Breakfast the Greens are competitive in seats Labor has held for 99 years, showing the “Greens surge is coming” amid disaffection with Labor.
double quotation markWhat people are telling me is that they are just so dismayed and disappointed at how Labor has moved away from their traditional values.
They have really followed the Liberals and One Nation down a rightwing rabbit-hole, and people are sick of that.

They don’t want politicians that just keep taking donations from big corporations and then giving handouts to the gas industry or giving into the gambling industry, or rolling out the red carpet for datacentres like Labor has done.
And that’s why they’re telling me that they’re voting Greens because they actually want a progressive voice that’s going to stand up for the values that this community cares about.
Jess Wilson and Ben Carroll ‘confident’ as they cast votes

My colleague Benita Kolovos has informed me that the premier, Ben Carroll, voted at his old primary school St Christophers in Airport West, while the Liberal leader, Jess Wilson, voted at Our Lady of Good Counsel primary school in Deepdene.
Wilson told a reporter at the polling booth she was “confident of the victories statewide today” and downplayed what it would mean for her to become the first elected female premier in Victoria.
double quotation markIt’s not about me. If I’m given that honour, we’re absolutely ready and I’m ready. But this is about Victorians and fixing this state.
Carroll told reporters he was “fighting every day” for the state. He said:

double quotation markI am confident because I’m getting that message. I’ve got it all day yesterday. People do feel like they’ve been sold down the river by the Liberal party, after 50% of Victorians voted, to come out with a radical privatisation agenda around kinder, renewables and water. People do feel very angry about that.

Going into the election, the Labor government is led by the premier, Ben Carroll. Carroll, who has only led Labor since late July, became leader after a spill against Jacinta Allan. Allan herself only became leader after the resignation of Daniel Andrews, who led Labor to the “Dan-slide” of 2022.

Victorian Labor has never won an election after changing leaders and this time they have done it twice. But Carroll has made an effort to distance himself from his predecessors saying, “I will do things differently”.
Jess Wilson is the Liberal leader, hoping to become the next premier. She became leader after a period of instability in the Victorian Liberal party that saw three leaders since the last election.
If she wins, she will be the youngest person to lead Victoria and the first woman to be elected premier. (Both Joan Kirner and Jacinta Allan became premier after their leaders resigned).
The Victorian Greens are led by Ellen Sandell. In 2014, she became the first Greens MP to be elected to Victoria’s lower house after campaigning against local toll roads.

Sandell hopes to take a page from progressive leaders around the world such as the New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani. At the News24 leaders’ debate, Sandell outperformed Ben Carroll, according to an audience poll.

Leading the insurgent One Nation is Warren Pickering. He is running in the marginal Labor seat of Pakenham in Melbourne’s outer east. The former Australian army combat engineer was also a unsuccessful One Nation Senate candidate.
At the News24 leaders’ debate, Pickering was outperformed by Sandell but audiences still preferred him over Carroll.
The Coalition is poised to win 55 of 88 lower-house seats according to a YouGov poll of more than 4300 voters, commissioned by the Herald Sun and News24 and published on election eve.
One Nation would gain 12 seats and the Greens would add five more MPs to their pack of three, according to the analysis conducted between 6 and 23 November.
A Newspoll reported by The Australian late on Thursday had the Coalition extending to a 15-point lead over Labor on a two-party preferred basis.
The Coalition’s lead of 57.5% to Labor’s 42.5% compares with the Coalition’s 55-45 lead in October before the election campaign began.
If the polls are correct the Victorian Greens will have their most successful campaign on record, gaining between 13% and 17% of primary votes.
The party leader, Ellen Sandell, received the second-highest approval rating among undecided voters during the campaign’s only four-way leaders debate on 17 November.
Good morning, and welcome to the Victorian election live blog.
I’m Josh Taylor and I will be taking you through until later this afternoon.

Going into today, polls suggest the Coalition will comfortably win majority government, while Labor faces an electoral wipeout after 12 years in government, with suggestions the premier, Ben Carroll, could lose his own seat.
More than 2.2 million people had already voted as of Friday, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission, meaning nearly half of those eligible have already cast their vote.
Just as well, too, given the weather in Victoria today. Those democracy sausage sandwiches will be a little wet today with all the rain.

There is a flood warning for parts of west, central and north-east Victoria, with possible minor flooding from Saturday morning for rivers including the Yarra. Rain is likely to continue throughout the day, easing into the evening with up to 30mm of rain expected in Melbourne.

items.title: 'I don't know what I'd do without it': Why shoppers and staff fear losing Poundland
paragraphs: Charlie visits Poundland almost daily and buys everything from toiletries to sweets
For Charlie Franklyn, a trip to Poundland is almost as routine as going to work.
The care worker from Teesside pops into her local branch nearly every day – it's where she buys cleaning products, beauty bargains and the budget-friendly finds she loves sharing online.
Charlie has been creating social media content for five years, and Poundland is one of her regular filming spots.

Her videos showcasing the store and its wares have proved popular, and although she's never been paid by the retailer, she's been gifted products over the years and built relationships with staff who invite her in to film.
"For me, Poundland is more than just a shopping stop. I buy so many things from there that are much cheaper than in other shops."

The budget retailer has gone into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk in the run-up to Christmas. For now, its 600 stores continue to trade as usual but they will eventually close if a buyer can't be found to rescue some or all of the business.
Charlie says she was "surprised by the news" and is worried about what it could mean for shoppers like her.
"With the cost-of-living crisis going on, places like Poundland are so important and we really don't need empty shops on the high street," she tells the BBC.
Kimi recently lost her job in retail and says she knows what a difficult time this must be for staff

Other shoppers the BBC spoke to are equally concerned. Kimi Browne, 26, from London, doesn't often shop at Poundland but relies on it for seasonal bargains, including Halloween decorations and accessories for her clothes.
She says the retailer is "an important part of the community as it offers affordable products for families".
Rea Catedrilla has a friend who works at the Poundland store in Notting Hill and feels "sad and sorry" for those who could lose their jobs.
She visits Poundland around four times per week because "it's less expensive than other shops and it's very convenient".
Rea is worried for her friend who works at Poundland in Notting Hill
Poundland opened its first store in Burton-upon-Trent in 1990 and grew into one of the UK's best-known discount retailers, with 900 shops across the country at its peak.
But rising costs and competition from supermarkets such as Aldi and Lidl put pressure on the business and, in June 2025, it was sold to US investment firm Gordon Brothers for a nominal £1.

There had been signs of a recovery – Poundland made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, compared with a £68m loss the previous year. But Gordon Brothers insists the business has missed its budget forecasts and would continue to struggle even if only its worst-performing stores were closed.
Aboud says locals and tourists are continuing to visit his store in Camden despite the news

News of the administration has left many Poundland staff on edge. Aboud, 39, who manages the Camden branch in north London, says it feels like a "slap in the face", as he thought the chain had started to recover over the last 18 months.
"Everything we've worked hard for was for nothing. Someone has come in and dismantled all that effort."
Aboud says his colleagues at the store have been emotional and that it's "very worrying to have a job at risk given the current climate".
But he adds that his team "are still hopeful" that a buyer could rescue the chain and that they continue to give "100% regardless of the circumstances".
Poundland opened in 1990 and had around 900 stores in the UK at its peak in the late 2000s
Retail expert Mary Portas said that when Poundland first opened, it was "everything under one roof that you didn't even know you wanted or needed" but it failed to keep pace as the market evolved.
While inflation has made it harder to sustain the £1 pricing model, other discount retailers have also made value shopping a more appealing experience, she says.
"Value brands, instead of looking shabby, which quite frankly Poundland often did, have taken themselves into a much better place," she says.
"On so many levels, Poundland just felt like yesterday's business."

The company has now appointed consultancy AlixPartners to oversee a sale of part or all of the discount retailer. Administrators will decide whether to sell the business as a whole or break it up, with the latter considered the more likely outcome.
Helen is hopeful that someone will buy Poundland and the stores will be saved
Helen Howes, Poundland's store manager in Camborne, Cornwall, says she wishes staff "could have been told more at times".
She adds that losing Poundland would be "devastating" for the town as it's one of its larger shops and an important draw for shoppers.
Jilly, who shops at the branch in Ealing, says the store has been a "godsend" and that it would be a blow to the local community if it closed.
Her shopping trolley is filled with everything from cleaning products and stationery to "upmarket things that I will gift for Christmas".
"It's tragic, everyone losing their jobs just before Christmas," she adds.

items.title: Should I get a flu vaccine now?
paragraphs: Health officials are urging more people to take up the offer of a free flu vaccine as the number of hospital patients seriously ill with the virus has risen sharply in the past week.
The flu surge has come slightly early this year but that is not completely unusual.
Flu activity is still at "moderate levels" and the peak may not arrive until December or early January, health officials warn.
So what is the advice on getting a vaccine, who can get it for free and who should pay?
"If you're offered it, it's a good idea to have it," says Prof Nick Hopkinson, professor of respiratory medicine at Imperial College London.
"The main reason is to avoid serious complications in vulnerable groups – so as many as possible should have it in those groups.
"People don't understand it's a potentially life-threatening infection and that the vaccine is safe."

Flu is a viral infection which affects the nose, throat and lungs. Often it goes away on its own but it can make people seriously ill – complications can include pneumonia, heart attacks and other underlying illnesses getting worse.
In England last winter, UKHSA estimated there were 3,798 deaths attributed to influenza.
Scientists have to predict which strains of influenza will be circulating before the vaccine is manufactured each year in time for winter.
The current one protects against three strains – two influenza A strains and one influenza B strain.
Even if these strains drift slightly, experts say getting vaccinated is still a good idea to lower the risk of severe illness.

Millions of vulnerable people are eligible for the free jab to help protect them against flu, including children, pregnant women, care home residents, people with lung conditions and anyone aged 65 and over.
But only around a third of under-65s and two-thirds of those aged 65 and over have been vaccinated so far this winter.
That leaves around seven million people unprotected at present, health officials say.
Parents are being urged to vaccinate young children in order to protect them and other people they come into contact with.
Yes. The vaccine does not rule out the possibility you will get flu, but it does reduce the chances you'll become very ill with it and end up in hospital.
It takes two weeks for your body's immunity to build up after being vaccinated, which is another reason to have the jab sooner rather than later.
Protection from the vaccine reduces the risk of serious flu complications by 50%, says Prof Hopkinson.
If you are not eligible for the free flu vaccine, you can still buy it from most pharmacies for between £15 and 25.
"It's a reasonable thing to consider," says Prof Hopkinson.
But it is far more important for the millions of vulnerable people offered it free to be vaccinated.
They are known to be at risk of health complications from the virus.
Other groups are also at risk: "Smokers are five times more likely to get flu – so quit now," he suggests.
There are different vaccines for those getting it free on the NHS and those paying for it privately.
However, the vaccines do the same job and protect against the same strains of flu.
Pharmacist Olivier Picard says he's seen a "massive spike in demand" for flu jabs in the last 24 hours.
More people are booking an appointment for a free vaccine they have already been reminded about, and others are asking about paying for it themselves.
"When it gets cold, people tend to wake up to getting the free jab and want it before Christmas," he says.
He says there is no issue with supplies of the vaccine at present and "plenty in the system".

items.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
paragraphs: The Canadian man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries apologised in court to the families of the victims, saying he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them.
Kenneth Law made the remarks on Friday during a sentencing hearing where prosecutors asked a judge to give him a 25-year prison term.

The 61-year-old pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.
He will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths under a plea deal which saw Canadian authorities withdraw more serious charges of murder.
During Friday's sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, prosecutors stressed that many of his victims were young and struggling with mental distress.
If Law receives the prosecution's recommended sentence, he would serve just under 20 years in prison, after accounting for credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest.
As she sought to make her case in court on Friday, Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty described Law as a predator taking advantage of "vulnerable people".
"What they needed was help. But what they found was Mr Law and his products for death," Doherty said.
She also said Law's motives were financial.

"If people could pay, he sold it to them. There's no discussion or inquiries or anything going on whereby Mr Law would have any ability to appreciate the circumstances of the individual he was dealing with," she said.
Law's defence lawyer, Matthew Gourlay, countered those claims, arguing that his client was not responsible for any of their battles with mental illness..

"Each of these incidents is its own unique tragedy," Gourlay said. "Mr Law may be a common denominator between them, but Mr Law was not the cause of the struggles and hardships that caused all these victims to seek out his products in the first place."
He said Law held a "misguided belief" he was helping his victims
Law's defence attorney has asked the court to give him a 12-year sentence.
At the end of the hearing, Law told the court that he had deep regret for aiding in the suicide deaths of his victims.
"To the families of the victims, words can never replace the loss of your loved ones. I convey my deepest condolences. I remain remorseful. I'm sorry."
The sentencing hearing followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court of the pain Law had caused.
Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date.
Authorities said the former chef sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients - who he met in online suicide forums - in 40 countries, roughly a quarter of which were sent to the UK.

items.title: Sony’s 1000XM4C headphones are a Black Friday bargain at $198
paragraphs: is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. That’s $100 off their October launch price.

There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up.

These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027.

items.title: Black Friday might be your one chance to get a portable SSD at a price you can almost afford
paragraphs: Black Friday has always been the best time of the year to buy a portable SDD. In fact, it was really the ONLY time to buy one if you could wait out the rest of the year because prices would routinely fall to 30% off if not more.

Today, that's more true than ever with SSD prices through the roof because of the component crunch triggered by demand from AI data centres. If 2026's eye-watering prices have caused you to spend the last few months having to desperately delete old raw photos and log footage to make room on your storage, now's your time to do something about it.

My top recommendation is the 2TB Samsung T7 reduced by 29% from $489.99 to $349.99 at Amazon and at B&H Photo. That's a discount of $140 off the current MSRP. The price is still a lot higher than it was 12 months ago, but it might be the best we see until the next big sale, i.e., Black Friday 2027.

items.title: This purple electric Chinese minivan can go up to 559 miles on a charge
paragraphs: is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget.

Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW’s ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023, China’s BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity.

It’s called the BYD Whale, and some back-of-the-napkin math suggests it lives up to the name. The van would be bigger than a Honda Odyssey, bigger than a Chrysler Pacifica, and bigger than a Toyota Sienna, at 17.3 feet (5,270mm) long, 6.5 feet (1,996mm) wide, 6 feet (1,815mm) tall, and with a 123-inch (3,130mm) wheelbase.

According to an auto-translated press release, the vehicle should have room for seven passengers and seven suitcases at a time, not that the company has shown off its interior yet. You can see a prominent sensor cluster on its forehead, though, and it’ll come equipped with LiDAR for advanced hands-free driving.

CarNewsChina points out it’s actually not the first with 900 km of CLTC battery range on board — Geely’s all electric Zeekr 009 minivan also claims to offer up to 900 km of range in one configuration. But BYD’s also claiming the can charge its battery from 10 percent to 97 percent in just nine minutes, and it get you from 10 percent to 70 percent in five minutes, according to Electrek.

The Whale will also come in a 248-mile (400 km) plug-in hybrid version as well, and the company’s planning to ship it in China in Q1 of 2027 for around 300,000 yuan. That’s roughly $45,000. As we’ve reported, Chinese cars are becoming quite competitive. Will they make it to the US?

items.title: The best robot vacuums we’ve tested are up to 60 percent off for Black Friday
paragraphs: writes about tech news, reviews gadgets, and helps readers save money by highlighting deals and product recommendations for The Verge.

Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself.

This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28, for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. If none of those are quite what you’re looking for, we’ve also found good deals on models from Roborock, Dreame, and more, with picks below for a variety of budgets and cleaning needs.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

The Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent robot vacuum for hardwood floors. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and a good vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most models. Read our review.

Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.

The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.

With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.

The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

The Freo X Ultra features spinning triangular mop pads and can swing slightly to reach baseboards. Its large charging dock holds two big water tanks, while Narwal’s disposable onboard bin compresses the dust. It’s also relatively quiet when it returns to the dock, and its anti-tangle brush and 8,200Pa of suction perform well on most carpets.

items.title: Yooka-Laylee’s free upgrade is skipping Xbox
paragraphs: is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Playtronic Games is getting ready to launch Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition as a free update on PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and PC on December 15th. Unfortunately for Xbox owners, the developer says it “can’t commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future.” In a statement posted on X, Playtronic said that it understands the frustration some players may feel, but that bringing the Definitive Edition to Xbox just isn’t viable “given the technological challenges and costs,” and reminded people that they’re a small team.

Some, like The Game Business editor-in-chief Christopher Dring, have speculated that Xbox’s smaller install base has made it harder for some indie devs to “financially justify” launching on Xbox. Others, like John Linneman of Digital Foundry, have countered that Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is ultimately a minor update and pointed out that the Xbox Series X version was already available in native 4K, unlike the PS4 and Switch versions.

items.title: Many of our favorite Blu-ray movies are over 50 percent off for Black Friday
paragraphs: Deck the shelves with discounted films, box sets, animated series, and more at some of the lowest prices we’ve seen.
Deck the shelves with discounted films, box sets, animated series, and more at some of the lowest prices we’ve seen.
is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

No shade to those who love their subscription services, but viewing physical movies is a time-honored tradition that shouldn’t go away. Watching them doesn’t feel all that different, but deciding which movie to watch feels less annoying; sifting through a movie collection on your shelf or in a storage binder is so much more fun (and less overwhelming) than scrolling endlessly in apps.

While standard Blu-ray players that display movies at up to 1080p are fairly inexpensive, 4K Blu-ray counterparts that can show movies in all their 4K HDR glory are significantly pricier (but totally worth it if you’re a movie buff). No matter the player you own, there are always Blu-ray deals, and the discounts are especially good during Black Friday. We’ve highlighted some of our favorites below, though Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and Gruv are each overflowing with more deals than we could realistically wedge into our coverage.
The once-Netflix-exclusive animated film is now available on 4K Blu-ray at a great price.
Akira Kurosawa’s High and Low showcases how capitalism can rot our moral compasses.
Ryan Coogler’s Sinners delivers a memorable plot with some fantastic mid-movie dance choreography. This movie’s part of Gruv’s “3 for $33” sale.
Own the complete run of The Next Generation across 41 discs in 1080p resolution, currently the most hi-res option available.
One of the best Black Friday deals, bar none. The set includes the theatrical cuts of the trilogy, plus the extended editions.
Setting aside that not every Matrix movie is amazing, the Déjà Vu set includes them all for less than if you bought them separately.
One of Rob Reiner’s many classics, but the only one with a truly fantastic, feisty line read from Mandy Patinkin.
All three of Richard Linklater’s Before movies in one set, a remarkable achievement that shows the evolution of a romantic relationship over decades.
Christopher Nolan’s time-jumping adventure is a must-watch that’s still enjoyable after multiple viewings.
The 1956 samurai tale is all about banding together to become something bigger. This set includes the recent 4K restoration.
A 4K collection that includes director John Singleton’s acclaimed films Boyz n the Hood, Poetic Justice, and Baby Boy.
All 26 episodes of the influential mecha anime in one set, plus a bunch of extras, including feature films, music videos, cast auditions, and more.
The Wachowski sisters followed up their work as directors on the Matrix trilogy to create this awesome live-action take on the classic manga.
If you liked the first Super Mario Bros. Movie, there’s more family-friendly fun where that came from in its follow-up.
It couldn’t have been easy to follow Ridley Scott’s original Blade Runner, but director Denis Villeneuve knocked it out of the park.
The beloved animated series came to Blu-ray in early 2026, giving viewers a more hi-res option after having to settle for DVD for over a decade.

items.title: The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
paragraphs: Apple’s most portable tablet offers a larger OLED screen and water resistance.
Apple’s most portable tablet offers a larger OLED screen and water resistance.
writes about tech news, reviews gadgets, and helps readers save money by highlighting deals and product recommendations for The Verge.

We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date.

The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.

The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify.

items.title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip
paragraphs: The Princess of Wales's personal account of her experience of cancer has a soul-bearing, emotionally candid tone never presented before in a royal documentary.

Discussing it at a private screening, she said it reflected the "fear, anxiety, uncertainty" shared by hundreds of thousands of people each year "who receive the words no one wants to hear" about having cancer.
The documentary, Heal, being shown on BBC One on Sunday, couldn't be further away from a stiff upper lip.
This is royal television without any palaces or carriages, it's an intense 30 minutes examining how "cancer strips everything away" and then a different kind of self-awareness emerges.
It reveals more of Catherine's inner thoughts than any of her previous speeches and we hear more from her children than ever before.
"Cancer does change you. It changes your body, it changes you physically. You have to go through treatment and surgeries and everything.

"But there's a much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you. I think when you've had to confront your own vulnerabilities, you know, when you're faced with your own mortality, you have to accept that life is not infinite and in those moments, yes, a shift does happen," she says.

Some viewers might be left in tears, others may think it's too schmaltzy - either way, they're going to be talking about it. It packs an emotional punch, even though it's more of a self-scripted, video diary than a conventional, journalistic documentary.

"This will be a documentary that most people can relate to and will admire her for doing. There is an emotional directness that's an unusual departure," says royal commentator Prof Pauline MacLaran, of Royal Holloway, University of London.
MacLaran thinks it will connect well with the public, who will admire Catherine's "bravery".

The documentary follows Catherine's Three Peaks Challenge, in which she climbed the biggest mountains in England, Wales and Scotland in a single day, and the cameras record her driving in between and her encounters with other climbers.
This climb is a big mountainous metaphor for the difficulties, resilience and help of other people during the "scary, disorientating experience" of her treatment.

At the summit of one peak she gets voice messages from her three children - George, Louis and Charlotte - who each in turn send their love in a way that shows the closeness of their family. They also all hug and kiss later, along with Prince William, with tears being brushed away.
Those moments could be the emotional peaks that people will share, in a documentary made for the social media age.
It's also probably the most we've heard directly from the royal children.

Somewhere, the late Prince Philip will be scratching his head at how much the royals have dropped their tradition of privacy. Although we don't learn from the film the type of cancer or any details of Catherine's treatment.
"No previous generation of the Royal Family would have considered producing something like this," says Valentine Low, author and royal commentator.
"They would have been less willing to talk about illness and personal matters," he says.
But this documentary is in keeping, says Low, with a generation "that's more likely to think in terms of whether there could be a positive message from the experience".
Nonetheless, says Low, such a film-making approach, sharing their own chosen thoughts with the camera without an interviewer, still allows Catherine to "control the narrative".

And there are questions that arise. She speaks of her cancer journey being a "pilgrimage" and the need to "spend time on our spiritual health" - and it makes you wonder whether there has been a deeply religious or spiritual experience as part of her recovery.

There's a melancholy tone to the documentary, describing the impact of a "really dark time", and you wonder how this will sit alongside the expectations of her future royal life, when she will be queen.

It could also raise wider questions about the treatment, waiting times and recovery support available to the great majority of NHS patients, who do not have royal titles, but whose needs are as intense.

But we see Catherine in this documentary in hospital wards sharing experiences with other cancer patients and hearing about their hopes and fears. It's deliberately raw and unadorned in how it's presented.
There are lighter moments too, joking with her brother James as they head up the mountains.

Speaking at a screening, Catherine said the documentary was about "giving back" to people facing similar health worries and also to recognise the support of health services and charities working with patients and families.
Proceeds from the documentary, like her Three Peaks Challenge fundraiser, will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, in support of the hospital where she received treatment.
The open, empathetic tone of the documentary has been warmly welcomed by those working with cancer patients.

"Watching someone speak so openly about the fear, the hope and the long road to recovery can make a real difference to those going through it," says Michelle Mitchell, chief executive of Cancer Research UK.
"Her honesty will help many people feel less alone, and it will encourage important conversations about cancer in homes across the country."
Ceinwen Giles, co-chief executive of Shine Cancer Support, said: "The film's honesty is what makes it so powerful.

"By being open about her experience, the princess gives others a way to start their own conversations about how cancer affects every part of a person's life, particularly younger adults and those with young families."
Catherine herself says that her experience has made her think about well-being in a much more holistic way, "not just about fixing what is wrong. It is about finding balance in how we live."
"My hope is that this film will encourage compassion, showing the real value in standing alongside one another in the hardest of times," she says.

Heal will be shown on BBC iPlayer from 12:00 GMT and BBC One at 18:40 GMT on 29 November. It will also air internationally, including on NBCUniversal in the US on 30 November, Channel 9 in Australia on 1 December and CTV and Noovo in Canada on 7 December

items.title: The little Welsh town that transformed a Strictly star's career
paragraphs: Strictly Come Dancing star Layton Williams has credited living and working in a small Welsh town with transforming his career.
The Bad Education actor spent months in Mold, Flintshire, rehearsing for the role of Angel in the musical Rent, which he said marked a turning point in his career.
"I've got to be honest, before I lived in Mold, I had not a clue that Mold was a place that existed, but I completely fell in love with it," he said.
Williams, from Bury in Greater Manchester, feels so connected to the town that he insisted on having a show at the Theatr Clwyd on his upcoming tour, Layton Live.
"The producers were like, 'we've never had a specific request to go to Mold, but we will make it happen'. And I said 'Thank you'," Williams said in an interview with Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales.
The show marks the 20th anniversary of his stage debut and is a "whistle-stop musical tour" through his career, which includes musicals such as Everybody's Talking About Jamie and Cabaret.
Olivier Award-winning Williams began acting professionally in theatre aged 12, but it was in Mold where he had his first major theatre role as an adult and his unlikely love for the town began.
"There was a shift while I was there. I learned so much doing the part," he said.
"I remember it so clearly, I stayed in this gorgeous little cottage, I just had such a wonderful time there."
Williams built such a connection with Mold's Theatr Clwyd that he became an ambassador and believes he even has a seat named after him in the auditorium.
In 2025, the actor earned his Olivier Award for Best Supporting Actor in a Musical, performing opposite Port Talbot theatre star Lauren Drew in Titanique - a musical parody of the film Titanic.
The actor, who played the iceberg while Drew portrayed Celine Dion, said the pair went on an "incredible journey" together and are still good friends.
"I'm actually going to her wedding next year and I'm going to see if she can come and have a little sing song with me in Wales," he said.
Williams met his partner James, from Wrexham, at Glastonbury Festival in 2023.
It was the year that Elton John performed there, who also wrote the music for Billy Elliot.
Williams said there are many "lovely connections with Elton" in his life, including beginning his career playing Billy Elliot in London's West End.

items.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
paragraphs: If he gets to form a government this time, it will be with the support of anti-immigration party Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, whose final rally took place in front of thousands of people in a bull-ring in Valencia on Spain's east coast.
The venue was filled with Spanish flags and green Vox banners, and one of the biggest cheers of the night came when the secretary general of the party called for "less burka and less halal".
Ignacio Garriga said he was not acting out of hatred but love for the homeland.
A small section of the crowd could be heard chanting "Viva Franco" in reference to the dictator, whose death in 1975 heralded the start of Spain's transition to democracy.
A number of first-time voters at the rally said they were supporting Vox because of its policies on immigration.
Lledó, 18, said what had happened in Ceuta in the summer, when more than 70,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco, showed Sánchez was not able to control the country's border.
She had come to the bullring with her mum and aunt, Carli Chilet, who argued that Vox "are the best for women's rights".

Vox is hoping to almost double its seats from the 33 it won three years ago. It backs policies such as "national priority" - putting Spanish citizens first for welfare - and "remigration" for foreigners not considered to be contributing to the economy.

While the conservatives tried to turn the spotlight on the series of scandals that have overshadowed the Socialists' term in office, Sánchez and his left-wing ally Ada Colau, who heads Frente Amplio (The Broad Front), focused on women's rights.

The two leaders seized on a moment in the debate when the PP leader accused Colau and the rest of the left of staying quiet during a flood disaster in Valencia, briefly moving his finger to his lips. The word he used "calladita" is a diminutive and can also be used to tell a woman to "keep quiet" in a condescending manner.
Sánchez reacted immediately and called on him to show "a little respect", accusing him of sexism.

Feijóo sought to clarify what he meant on Friday, and accused Ada Colau of remaining silent during "these years of corruption". His decision to wind up his campaign in Seville was significant, because the wider southern region of Andalusia has 61 seats in Spain's 350-seat parliament, more than any other.
Andalusia is also important because it is run by a coalition made up of the PP and Abascal's Vox, as are three other regions, Extremadura, Aragón, and Castilla y León.
Feijóo has insisted he wants to govern with a majority, backed up by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox and says he has never spoken to Abascal about giving Vox ministerial power.
"Governing is about managing, and I have spent my whole life preparing for this moment," he said in Seville.

One of his new supporters at the rally was a retired woman called Isabel who told Spanish public broadvaster RTVE that she was attending a PP rally for the first time. The formerly loyal Socialist voter said she was "disillusioned" with a party led by Sánchez. Another voter at the rally said Spain needed "a good manager".
Sánchez took to the stage in Madrid with his wife Begoña Gómez, and donned a red T-shirt that read "power of the people".
He then went on to praise Colau and her left-wing coalition's campaign.
"These elections are about moving Spain forward, not taking it backwards," he said.

Socialist supporter Leon Felipe, 25, told Reuters news agency: "Well, I think what's at stake in these elections is a big deal, is not a change of government... but rather a return to the past - a return to Franco's dictatorship.
"So, I believe that young must mobilise."
As he was speaking, Colau told a large audience in the south of Madrid that not only would they "not remain silent, we will win", vowing to form another "progressive government".

items.title: Allstate has been suffering an outage since Monday
paragraphs: One of the biggest insurance companies in the country has been dealing with a major outage for five days.
One of the biggest insurance companies in the country has been dealing with a major outage for five days.
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

On Monday, November 23rd, Allstate began dealing with an outage that has impacted its website, mobile apps, and roadside assistance service. It’s just the latest company, including Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, to suffer an outage in the last few weeks. As of Friday afternoon, access to accounts through the app and site appeared to still be down. When asked for comment, the company pointed us to a notice on its site reading:

Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.

Opening the app pops up a notification saying the company is working to “restore access as soon as possible,” and encourages customers to contact the company by phone to file and manage claims. Users have flooded X and Reddit with complaints about the outage, some of whom have either been left waiting for roadside assistance or have been unable to insure new vehicles.
Allstate hasn’t publicly identified a cause for the outage.

items.title: The 25 best gaming deals we’ve found so far for Black Friday
paragraphs: While deals on consoles and key PC components are in short supply during Black Friday (or simply not good enough to warrant covering), there are numerous fantastic discounts on video games, accessories, and monitors to make up for it. We thought it’d be useful to display all of the deals we think are worth your attention on one page instead of sprinkled here and there in our coverage.

Below, you’ll find the very best discounts we’ve found for PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC players to shop. You can filter the table below to display exactly the type of products you’re looking for.
Both the white and midnight black versions of the DualSense Edge are discounted. Refurbished versions (with the same warranty as new controllers) are another $25 off.

The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Pauline’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

The Pro 3 features swappable ABXY face buttons and joystick caps, providing players with a highly customizable experience. It also features new L4 and R4 macro buttons between the triggers and its USB-C charging port, along with more durable and power efficient TMR joysticks.

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.
The Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition includes both the base game and the “Shadow of the Erdtree” expansion, along with new customization options.
The Fractal Scape gaming headset has a sleek, refined design, with a 2.4GHz low-latency connection and excellent sound for gaming or music.

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

The Nex Playground is a motion-controlled console that connects to your TV and uses a built-in camera and AI to track your movements as you play. Designed for ages five and up, it comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whac-a-Mole. You can download more games, including titles featuring popular characters like Elmo, with a paid Play Pass subscription.
The World of Warcraft Celebration Pass cuts the price of a 12-month subscription during Black Friday, offering access to World of Modern WoW, WoW: Forever, and WoW: Classic at a discounted rate.

The Witcher 3 lets you explore the war-torn Northern Kingdoms as Geralt of Rivia while preparing to face the mysterious Wild Hunt. The recent remaster adds improved visuals, smoother combat, and better movement, cementing the game’s status as one of the best RPGs of all time.

Clicking the Superstrike feels like using a regular gaming mouse, which is impressive considering there are no mechanical switches inside. Instead, it uses haptics to emulate the effect (to great effect).

One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.
Make this the year that the gamer in your life has an OLED TV to play their console games on. Despite being affordable, the B6E doesn’t skimp on features.

A gift for the gamer who already has all the gear they need (and who loves to read about gaming when they’re not gaming). The site focuses on well-researched deep dives and oral histories on classic video games.
The 1440p 240Hz refresh rate screen is sleek, but pretty basic for the price. It stands out, though, thanks to its DualSense-charging cradle that extends from its bottom. This is the first discount.
If you’re seeking out a prettier DualSense, the Chroma series of controllers are just a few bucks more than the standard color schemes.

No game has delivered more thrills per minute (TPM) this year than Star Wars Galactic Racer. Podracing is back, and it’s better than ever with this title’s stellar sense of speed, plus it has a surprisingly memorable cast of characters.

Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

Halo: Campaign Evolved lets you revisit the original Halo: Combat Evolved campaign with better graphics, updated controls, and improved sound. The well-crafted remake also adds three new missions starring Master Chief and Sgt. Johnson that take place before the main campaign. Read our review.

USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep you occupied for hours on end.
The MK.2 version of the standard Stream Deck comes with 15 programmable buttons, a swappable faceplate, and a detachable stand.

The latest entry in the long-running survival horror series returned in 2026, with two different styles of gameplay (tense first-person and guns-blazing third-person perspectives) via its dual protagonists. Read our review.

items.title: US backs IAEA authority to negotiate South Korean submarine safeguards after China objects
paragraphs: The United States says the International Atomic Energy Agency, the U.N. nuclear watchdog, has the authority to negotiate safeguards for South Korea’s planned nuclear-powered submarines, a State Department spokesperson told VOA.
The statement comes after China objected at an IAEA Board of Governors meeting last week, saying that all of the agency’s member states should agree before such talks proceed.

Safeguards are measures the IAEA uses to verify that nuclear material is not diverted for weapons purposes. Nuclear-powered submarines present a particular challenge because their fuel is used for a military activity rather than a peaceful nuclear activity, and the submarines can spend long periods at sea.
The United States approved South Korea’s plan to build nuclear-powered submarines in November 2025, but key details, including who will supply the fuel, have not been settled.

Under Article 14 of its safeguards agreement with the IAEA, a country without nuclear weapons can reach a separate arrangement with the agency that temporarily suspends normal safeguards on nuclear material used for permitted military purposes, such as powering submarines.

At the IAEA board meeting on November 18, China’s ambassador in Vienna, Li Song, said that the way in which the agency monitors nuclear fuel for South Korea’s submarines should be decided by the board and all member states, not only through technical talks between the IAEA and Seoul.

He also said U.S.-South Korean cooperation would be the second case, after AUKUS, involving the transfer of nuclear material for non-peaceful purposes. Under AUKUS, a 2021 pact, Britain and the United States are helping Australia acquire nuclear-powered submarines.
But a State Department spokesperson said in a written response to VOA that the IAEA has established authority to negotiate safeguards implementation, including Article 14 arrangements.

U.S. Ambassador Wells Griffith welcomed the technical consultations at the meeting, saying they match the IAEA’s existing authority and South Korea’s Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty obligations. The European Union praised Seoul’s reporting compliance, and the IAEA director general’s report, saying any finalized arrangement would be submitted to the board for appropriate action.

An initial IAEA report released November 18 said South Korea plans to manufacture the fuel domestically using imported low-enriched uranium, enriched to 20% or less, without naming a supplier. South Korea and the IAEA held their first technical consultation October 8 and plan to continue talks next year toward an Article 14 arrangement.

items.title: Charity founded in Captain Tom's name bids to be struck off
paragraphs: A charity set up by the family of renowned pandemic fundraiser Capt Sir Tom Moore has applied to be struck off.
The charity is now known as the 1189808 Foundation, having dropped Sir Tom's name at the request of his family last year.
An application to have it struck off appeared on the Companies House register on Friday.
The World War Two veteran became a household name during the first Covid-19 lockdown, raising £39.4m for NHS charities by walking laps of the garden at his home in Marston Moretaine, Bedfordshire.

However, the charity founded in his name became mired in controversy after the charities watchdog found misconduct and mismanagement on the part of his daughter and her husband in their running of it.

The Charity Commission's report uncovered a "repeated pattern of behaviour" through which Hannah Ingram-Moore and her husband, Colin, made private gains and which the regulator said would have left people feeling "misled".
A £1.4m book deal and an £18,000 awards ceremony appearance fee were among the financial benefits the Ingram-Moores were found to have enjoyed through the Captain Tom Foundation.
They have already been banned from being charity trustees and earlier resigned from the foundation.
The millions raised by the late Sir Tom and donated to NHS Charities Together before the foundation was formed were not part of the commission's inquiry.
The father-of-two died aged 100 in February 2021 with coronavirus.
