paragraphs: The work and pensions secretary has said an investigation is looking into a "serious cyber incident" affecting his government department.

items.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
paragraphs: One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.
The latest super-rugged wearable from Apple features better battery life than the previous version, plus AI-powered features like Siri Recap also available on the Series 12.

The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly, ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.

With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
The cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design.

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Acer’s answer to the MacBook Neo, with an Intel Core 5 processor, 8GB of RAM, 120Hz display, and speedy Thunderbolt 4 ports. We’re still testing this one, but it’s showing promise for an affordable choice.

Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.

Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

Roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.
The best XPS 13 in years. It doesn’t have a headphone jack and starts with only 8GB of RAM but it’s an excellent thin-and-light with a great screen, a solid Intel chip, and speedy storage.

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.
It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It also works with the new Aliro standard, making it compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.

Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.

The Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.

Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

The Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150 PSI.

These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they fit seamlessly into any major smart home platform. Best of all, the smart features come at a price that makes buying multipacks more affordable than other brands.
A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.

The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Fairphone’s latest is a very light update to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.

The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.
The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep mother dearest occupied for hours on end.

Google’s new Pixel 10A introduces faster wired charging, Satellite SOS, and new AI tools like Camera Coach and Auto Best Take. Otherwise, it’s basically the Pixel 9A, with the same Tensor G4 chip and a dual-camera system. Read our review.

There are many gaming headsets out there, but few as elegant as Fractal’s Scape. The PC-focused (but Switch- and PlayStation-compatible) wireless headset offer great sound and include a wireless charger, and they have easy-to-master physical controls.

Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power after storms hit US on Thanksgiving
paragraphs: Hundreds of thousands of people are without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.
Conditions are now expected to improve, though forecasters caution that it will take some time. The West Coast has also been affected by its own storms.
Flight disruption also persists, with hundreds more delays and cancellations reported on Friday - which is expected to be another busy travel day.
More than 2,500 flights within, into or out of the US were delayed on Thursday, and more than 450 were cancelled, according to Flightaware.com.
One passenger told the BBC he had been stuck at New York's LaGuardia Airport for 13 hours while trying to fly to see friends in Chicago for Thanksgiving.
Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the East Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.
Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds, while waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.
On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.
Parts of some states are under states of emergency, including New York.
Nearly 2in (5cm) of rain fell on New York City's iconic Central Park, making it the wettest Thanksgiving on record at that site as well, according to preliminary data, external from the NWS.
Organisers of the city's annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have also pushed back the event to Saturday - marking the event's first postponement in its 100-year history.
In neighbouring New Jersey, there were multiple reports of closed roads and bridges, and images of floodwater blanketing city streets.
"This is wild," an Ocean City, New Jersey-based blogger said in a video, external posted on social media, as he waded through water splashing above his waist.

items.title: Body found in woodland confirmed as missing Kelsey Hunter
paragraphs: Police have confirmed that a body found in woodland near Springholm has been identified as Kelsey Hunter
Police have confirmed that a body found in woodland in southern Scotland has been identified as missing 20-year-old Kelsey Hunter.
She had last been seen in Castle Douglas at 17:00 on Saturday and a major search was carried out around the nearby village of Springholm where she lived.

On Tuesday, Daniel McKnight, 21, appeared on petition at Dumfries Sheriff Court charged with murder and two other charges, including defeating the ends of justice. Kelsey's body was found at about 19:15 on Wednesday.
McKnight made no plea and was remanded in custody.

The search operation around the Dumfries and Galloway village concluded when the body was found but police said extensive inquiries remained ongoing with a number of resources being used - including forensic specialists.
Det Ch Insp Stephen McGrath said: "Our thoughts remain with Kelsey's family at this incredibly difficult time, and we are continuing to provide them with support.
"They have asked that their privacy is respected.
"Extensive work remains ongoing and a team of officers are continuing to carry out inquiries."
Police said forensic specialists were still involved in their inquiries
He thanked everyone who had come forward with information so far and said officers would remain in the area while the investigation continued.
Door-to-door and CCTV inquiries are still being carried out.
Local area commander Emma Dodds said: "We understand how upsetting this has been for the local community, but we continue to have a significant amount of resources dedicated to this investigation.
He asked anyone with any concerns, or information to contact police, external.
Support has been offered at the primary school near where a cordon has been in place
A large police presence has been in the village - which sits next to the A75 that runs from Gretna to Stranraer - since Sunday evening.
Dogs, a helicopter and specialist officers were involved in the search while officers made door-to-door inquiries.
Dumfries and Galloway Council has been offering support to the village primary which is close to where a police cordon was in place.
It said a message had been sent to the community to reassure them that the school continued to be a "safe and nurturing space".
The local authority's principal education psychologist has also been working with the primary and Castle Douglas High School to "provide support to learners and staff".

items.title: Why snooker could be the most mentally challenging sport
paragraphs: The unique psychological challenges of elite level snooker
It is perhaps one of the most visceral and deeply human interviews that any sportsperson has ever given.

When Mark Allen, snooker's world number 11, spoke live on TNT Sports, external in October, he said he was in a "bad place", that he didn't see a future in the game, and that he was "just trying to survive".
Allen had just been beaten at the Northern Ireland Open. It was his first match since the World Championship, when in May he was one black ball away from a place in the final.

He has not spoken publicly since. In a post on social media in early November, Allen said the future is "looking brighter",, external although this week he explained he was having a "very tough" time, external and was "definitely stuck in a major low right now".
While Allen has not publicly discussed the reasons for his struggles, and if it is related to the sport, he had previously said "there is more to life than just a career".
And this would be far from the first time that poor mental health has affected a snooker player.
Right from the 1970s and the sport's first television boom, some of its great characters have spoken openly, and regularly, about addiction, isolation and snooker's unique psychological challenges.
So what is it about the sport that makes it so mentally difficult? And what is being done to help?
If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this story you can visit BBC Action Line, which has details of a range of advice and support.
In his emotional interview, Allen said he had spent 10 weeks in a mental health clinic and discharged himself to play in Belfast, though he planned to continue his treatment.
Other players have also previously spoken candidly about their own struggles, including multiple world champions Ronnie O'Sullivan and Mark Selby.
Selby considered retirement after a first-round defeat at the 2024 World Championship, while in 2025 O'Sullivan said many players "suffer in silence".

Snooker is, perhaps alongside golf, one of the most intensely individual sports, where players spend long hours alone in dimly lit practice rooms or travelling on the road, and where entire livelihoods can come down to tiny misjudgements.
"At least in golf you have your own ball. You don't have to worry about anyone else," 1997 world champion Ken Doherty told BBC Sport.
"In snooker, when you're sitting in your chair and your opponent is at the table, you can do nothing. Only sit and bear it.
"That is the toughest part about our sport and mentally that is quite difficult for people to comprehend."
Dr Paul Gaffney is a psychologist who has worked with Allen for the past four seasons. Snooker players, he says, can feel like they are inside a "colosseum".
"There are people looking down at you, and you can absolutely thrive, or be beaten in front of the world stage."
Gary Wilson, the world number 28, has also spoken openly about the bouts of depression he has suffered during his 22-year career.
"It's a very lonely sport," the 41-year-old told BBC Sport.
"You're practising in a club and you could be in there on your own for six, seven, eight hours a day in a dark room, with just a snooker light on.
"It can get unhealthy mentally in itself, but it's what you've got to do. You've got to dedicate yourself to it.
"I think it is a more mentally destructive sport, potentially, than a lot of other individual sports."
When asked how he felt watching Allen's interview, Wilson said: "We can all relate.
"There are a lot of lads who are a lot lower down on the tour struggling.
"Every couple of years, this coming out and nothing being done about it, isn't really good enough."
Emotional Allen tells the BBC he is contemplating retirement following NI Open exit

Since 2021, snooker's governing body, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA), has put mental health provisions in place for players in the form of a partnership with Sporting Chance, a charity founded by former Arsenal and England footballer Tony Adams.
In the five years since the partnership was formed, Sporting Chance has provided more than 180 sessions of counselling for a wide range of issues.

Players experiencing mental health issues are encouraged to ring a confidential 24/7 helpline, and Sporting Chance will then arrange free treatment with a qualified therapist. This can take place over six to 12 talking sessions.
But some players believe that support could go further. In an interview in January 2025, O'Sullivan and Selby said they would like to see mental health professionals operate on-site at tournaments.
"I think players would have a lot more inclination to use somebody physically there at tournaments. I don't know how feasible that is," said Wilson.

There are benefits and drawbacks to the Sporting Chance service. Players receive a bespoke counsellor, rather than one who may speak to every player, but they are required to reach out themselves for this through a helpline. Doherty, who sits on the WPBSA players' board, believes it is the best solution.
"Players don't necessarily want to go and speak to someone at a tournament," Doherty said.
"We thought about having someone on hand, but then we thought, we don't think anyone would use it.
"This is a free service. Nobody has to know. Nobody will know on the circuit. It's just you and the person you're talking to.
"I know Ronnie [O'Sullivan] and Mark [Selby] spoke about that, but they obviously didn't know that service was there for them, that it's free, and that it's available for the whole tour."
WPBSA chairman Jason Ferguson, a former professional player himself, said: "The highs are very high and the lows are very low.
"If there's anything we can work on, it's continually getting the message out to other players to say those services are there."
How Tony Adams' charity is helping snooker players - but could more be done?
In 2021, Wilson said he felt "totally gone" when the depression he explained he was suffering with came to a head in a match against John Higgins.
Wilson missed a pot, and while still down on his shot, thrashed the cue ball into a neighbouring red,, external sending the frame into chaos. He was fined £250 and received a formal warning.
But Wilson - known as the Tyneside Terror - believes there could be a more liberal approach to such displays of emotion in this most gentlemanly of sports.
"You're expected to keep your emotions completely in check at all times," he said.
"Now that's just not sport. When you look at any other sport that you play… you've got to be able to vent."
In response, Ferguson said that while snooker's authorities and fans love to see such passion, fundamentally it is a sport of "great etiquette".

Allen is next due to play in the UK Championship - a tournament he won in 2022 - which starts on Saturday. He has been drawn against qualifier Yuan Sijun but has not spoken publicly about whether he will play.
For Dr Gaffney, watching Allen's interview at Belfast's Waterfront venue was "painful". It made him feel "sadness, but also admiration".

"The brilliant thing about what he's done - his courage, his integrity, his class in the last few weeks - is there will be people watching snooker who wouldn't have been watching snooker before, because Mark Allen is playing," said Dr Gaffney, "and I think that says everything about the man."

items.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
paragraphs: In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

There were also many happy admissions of historical ignorance. Since taking on the Ukraine brief a year ago, Kushner said, he had to learn “the algorithm of Europe and how complicated that is”, and he had to get abreast of “the local issues with Ukraine”.

As a businessman he brought a special expertise, he claimed. “Look at what’s happening in the Middle East with sanctions, with Russia, with Iran. I think that you have to understand economics in order to understand geopolitics because the two go together very, very closely,” he said.
But the main revelation was how much he believes the Ukraine conflict is not a case of an aggressor and a victim – but is simply a series of misunderstandings and miscommunication.

Indeed, he treated Vladimir Putin as if he were a masterful corporate executive quite willing to close the deal if he were only given the right economic incentives – instead of a man ready to sacrifice hundreds of thousands of Russians to reclaim part of a historical empire.

In the process, Kushner revealed – often inadvertently – that he had largely bought into the Russian narrative of a string of postwar missteps by Europe and the US coming to a head in Nato’s expansion eastwards after 9/11.

That, in turn, has led him to adopt Moscow’s central demand to reshape the European security order to allow Russia, without opprobrium, to retain land it has gained by force. Shining through his answers was a naive bias towards the aggressor, presented as a mediator’s desire to understand both parties.

Praise veering on awe for the Russian leader flowed. “Putin – people can like what he has done, they can not like what he has done – [but] he is a grand master of politics. He is a historic figure,” he said. Any sense that Putin may have blundered escaped him.

As to the rights and wrongs of invading another country, Kushner was blasé. “After all, most lines in Europe have changed over time and they are decided through war or peace, or concessions. It’s not about fairness or who is right or wrong. It’s about ending the killing,” he said.

He understood, too, why Putin could not offer a ceasefire: “He has very little confidence that if he stops the war, that he [will] be able to get to a postwar settlement that leads to not having a future war.”
To stop the killing, the killing has to go on.
What is more, Kushner was struck by the Russian leader’s self-control. “So far Putin has shown restraint and he has agreed not to use nuclear weapons and he has reassured us that is his intention.”

Kushner denied Trump had put any pressure on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, defying his interviewer to provide evidence – at which point Döpfner recited a list of examples, including only last month when the US president suggested that Ukraine should get a new leader.

Trump was “a strong counter-puncher”, argued Kushner, implying that Zelenskyy had thrown the first punch in a conflict that began with a Russian invasion. Relations with Ukraine were cooperative, he said before pointedly saying Kyiv needed things from the US, without which “Ukraine will not be safe in the future”.

After noting that “the territorial issue is now a little bit of a deadlock”, his strategic insight was that if a future security architecture for Europe could be agreed, the answer to the land question in Donbas would eventually follow.
In essence, he proposed a revival of the Russia-Nato council, one of the bodies eviscerated by Putin’s war.

He also envisioned Ukraine inside the European Union with security guarantees akin to those offered by Nato’s article five. Though it was impossible at this stage to give “more specificity” about these guarantees in the detailed way Ukraine sought, he admitted.
So far, neither Moscow nor Kyiv have bought this plan, let alone a wary Europe.

Kushner tried to be polite about Europe, insisting it had to be at the negotiating table, but he could not stop himself characterising European military assistance to Ukraine as a “proxy war” against Russia.

As an analysis of why the Ukraine war had not ended inside the 24 hours Trump had promised when he took office again, Kushner showed an alarming belief that the answer lay in granting more concessions to Putin, and that the misunderstandings and misperceptions would then evaporate.

items.title: Tory candidates must sign pledge to scrap net-zero targets, says Badenoch
paragraphs: All Conservative candidates will have to sign a pledge committing themselves to leaving the European Convention on Human Rights and scrapping net-zero emission targets ahead of the next election, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has said.
Unveiling her "candidates covenant" at an event in the East Midlands, Badenoch said both policies were "necessary for a stronger economy and a stronger country".
The move could see some senior Conservatives blocked from standing for the party at the next general election.
Lord Barwell, a former Conservative minister and No 10 chief of staff, said: "After a summer in which the impacts of climate change were clearer than ever, this is bad policy."
He added: "Given the seats Conservative strategists say they are targeting, it is also bad politics."

Tobias Ellwood, a former Conservative MP and defence minister, told Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5Live he had applied to stand as a candidate in the next election but had not passed what he described as "the purity test".

He criticised Badenoch's covenant, saying: "Can you imagine if... prior to the war, you had to sign up to [Neville] Chamberlain's 'peace in our time' speech, you know, [Winston] Churchill wouldn't have been allowed to stand."
"I mean, there must be times where you can have different views and different views within a party are actually helpful," he added.

Addressing party activists in Newark, Badenoch said: "The government that cleans up Andy Burnham's mess is going to have to make some very difficult decisions... it is not going to be for the faint-hearted.

"I need everyone who stands as a Conservative candidate at the next election to know what they are standing for - I don't want to hear complaining from MPs that they didn't know what we were going to do."
The covenant also states that candidates must support staying out of the EU, reducing the size of the state and changing the welfare system.
Sir Mark Spencer, a chief whip in the last Conservative government, became the first to sign the new pledge.
He lost his seat in the 2024 election, but is now standing in Newark, where he hopes to unseat the Conservative-turned-Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick.
A Labour spokesperson said: "Kemi Badenoch is living in an alternate reality. She says the Tories have changed but the truth is they're the same old Tories."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "Kemi Badenoch tells us the Conservative Party has changed - it's hard to believe when she's surrounded by so many Remainers and her party is selecting lots of failed ex-Tory MPs who got kicked out at the last election."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "The Conservatives pretend they care about winning back support from millions of former Conservative voters, yet Kemi Badenoch is now asking her candidates to sign the 'Farage pact'.
Both the commitments to leave the ECHR and repeal net-zero targets represent a shift from previous Conservative governments.

The net-zero target was originally legislated for by the Theresa May-led Conservative government in 2019. The party's 2024 manifesto said it was proud of its record on reducing emissions and remained "committed to delivering net-zero by 2050".
In the run-up to the election, then Prime Minister, and Conservative leader, Rishi Sunak resisted demands from some in his party to commit to leaving the ECHR.

Since becoming leader, Badenoch has argued that the net-zero target - which commits the UK to reducing its net greenhouse gas emissions to almost zero by 2050 - couldn't be achieved "without a serious drop in our living standards or by bankrupting us".

Last year, she also announced that, if elected, her party would take the UK out of the European Convention on Human Rights, the treaty that guarantees certain human rights such as the right to privacy, protection against torture and a right to a family life.
Badenoch said the convention prevented the UK from being able to secure its borders and deport foreign criminals.
Over the past year, the Labour government, along with other European countries have agreed to negotiate a new approach to the convention with the aim of making it easier to deport people.

items.title: Police look for more than 100 gig-goers to help Co-op Live probe
paragraphs: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from the arena during the rapper's concert
ByStewart Whittingham and Rachael LazaroNorth West
Police have said they are trying to contact more than 100 gig-goers to help their investigation after an unknown substance was released at a concert at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.
Detectives believe a "small group of organised criminals targeted people in the crowd to commit a series of robberies on the night".
More than 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday.
One woman was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood".
No arrests have been made and the substance has not yet been identified.
Acting Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "We're working to identify those [robbery] suspects and the substance that we believe was released in the crowd as part of these incidents.
He said there had been "similar incidents at two Don Toliver gigs in Europe that are also relevant to our enquiries".
Fans reported that a spray or gas was released into the crowd in Zurich and Paris.
Fans say they were in quarantine at the Etihad sports hall for about six hours

Jess Kinyata, 20, from West London, who was one of 12,000 people evacuated from the arena, said before the "gas began" his 18 carat gold chain, worth about £1,500, was stolen from him during a set by the concert's opening artist, Victony.
GMP previously said there had been nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert.
Harding said officers had been "working through footage captured on mobile phones and CCTV".
He added: "There are over a hundred people at the gig that we are working to try and contact to potentially assist with our enquiries.
"We thank all those that have assisted us so far.
"We also know many more people were impacted on the night and afterwards, physically and psychologically."
Joey Howe said there was confusion and panic when the show stopped
North West Ambulance Service said it had deployed crews, including its Hazardous Area Response Team, who carried out decontamination "as a precaution".
Those who suffered symptoms had been taken to the Etihad stadium.
Some fans complained the process, which involved them changing into paper white suits and putting their clothes in a plastic bag, was "invasive" and "traumatic".
Many stayed quarantined for several hours before being able to leave in the early hours of Monday.
GMP said: "People's safety, and the safety of the wider community, was at the forefront of officers' minds throughout."
Fans said the incident happened 30 to 40 minutes into the rapper's set
The substance was released at about 22:00 GMT, near the end of Toliver's show as part of his Nitrous – Octane world tour.
Concertgoers have described feeling "unsafe" and seeing "distressing" scenes and people "coughing up blood".
Posting on Instagram, Toliver said: "My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured.
"The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my fans."
Co-op Live, which reopened its doors on Thursday night for a gig by American singer Phoebe Bridgers, previously said its priority remained "the safety and security of all visitors" to the venue.

items.title: The best Black Friday deals on AirPods, MacBooks, and other Apple gear
paragraphs: We dug up the biggest price drops on Apple hardware and accessories, from tablets and laptops to chargers.
We dug up the biggest price drops on Apple hardware and accessories, from tablets and laptops to chargers.

Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, which have dropped to new lows.

In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.

The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review.

Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review.

The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review.

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

The Baseus PicoGo AM52 is a 10,000mAh magnetic power bank that supports fast 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging and up to 45W wired charging via its built-in USB-C cable. It was one of the fastest wireless chargers we tested, bringing an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65 percent in an hour. Read our guide to the best Qi2 batteries.
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad offers 128GB of storage — twice that of its predecessor — and runs on a faster A16 chip. It also comes in four colors: blue, pink, yellow, and silver.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Designed to pair with a Mac, the latest Apple Studio Display features a sharp 5K Retina display, a great 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that keeps you in frame during video calls, and a good six-speaker sound system with spatial audio. Sadly, it only offers two Thunderbolt 5 ports in addition to a pair of USB-C ports. Read our review.

items.title: Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez confident of election victory despite polls – as it happened
paragraphs: Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez said on Friday that he was convinced he would ⁠secure a left-wing majority ⁠in a snap ​general election despite adverse public polling, as the political parties prepared to wrap up campaigning ahead of Sunday’s vote, Reuters reported.

Amid a legal ban on publishing new ⁠opinion surveys, the Socialist leader insisted that internal data suggested his party would win the most votes, allowing him to clinch re-election with the support of smaller ⁠leftist allies.

“I can’t conceive of us losing,” Sanchez told radio station SER, adding that left-leaning voters were ​increasingly mobilising to turn out in droves, a ‌prerequisite for reaching a progressive ‌majority to tackle issues such as the country’s deep housing crisis.
double quotation mark“When progressive Spain gets going, it’s unstoppable.”

However, nearly all the polls released before ‌the ban showed a clear advantage for a potential coalition between the conservative People’s Party and far-right Vox, which seek to oust Sanchez after eight years in power.
Will Spain’s snap election in November bring a far-right party into government? - explainer
From mocked to mainstream: how Spain’s far-right Vox transformed its fortunes
Spain’s election: the end of a leftwing icon? - podcast
